summary: The PATCH handler parses the body and calls store.update inside a req 'end' callback, which the handler's try/catch does not cover. Invalid JSON or empty text throws an uncaught exception and crashes the server. I confirmed this at runtime: SyntaxError and StoreError both surfaced as uncaughtException. Opened src/server.mjs, src/store.mjs, src/client.mjs, test/helpers.mjs, test/notes.test.mjs and AGENTS.md. Grepped for update/PATCH (only server.mjs, store.mjs and the new test use them). npm test passes 7/7. Bob's PATCH on Alice's note correctly returns 404.

findings.issue: The code runs in an event callback after handle() has returned, so the surrounding try/catch never sees its errors. JSON.parse on a malformed or empty body throws SyntaxError. store.update throws StoreError(400) for empty, non-string or too-long text. A JSON body of `null` makes body.text throw a TypeError. Each of these is an uncaughtException that crashes the process (reproduced for '{nope' and {text:''}), and the client never gets a response. There is no req 'error' listener either. This breaks the house rule that a bad request returns a 4xx JSON error and never crashes the server.
findings.fix: Use the existing helper the way POST does: `const body = await readJson(req); return send(res, 200, store.update(note.id, body?.text))`. readJson turns bad JSON into StoreError(400) and handles req errors. Because it is awaited, StoreErrors from store.update reach the catch block and come back as 400.

findings.issue: Only the happy path is tested. Nothing covers the failure paths this change adds: PATCH with invalid JSON, empty text or too-long text should return 400 and the server should keep serving. Nothing checks that another user's PATCH returns 404 and leaves the text unchanged. A missing-token PATCH returning 401 is also untested. A test for any of the first three would have caught the crash above. House rule: every behavior change comes with a test.
findings.fix: Add tests modelled on the existing POST ones. PATCH with '{nope', {text:''} and {text:'x'.repeat(501)} each return 400, and a follow-up GET /notes still returns 200. Bob PATCHing Alice's note gets 404 and Alice's text is unchanged. PATCH without a token gets 401.

findings.issue: update assumes the id exists. `notes.get(id)` can be undefined, and then `note.text = text` throws a TypeError that becomes a 500. The only current caller checks existence first, but the store is exported and nothing in update itself enforces that. The same validation block is also copied from create.
findings.fix: Add `if (!note) throw new StoreError(404, 'not found')` after the lookup. Optionally move the text validation into a shared validateText(text) helper that create and update both call.

findings.issue: src/client.mjs says to keep it in step with server.mjs, but it has no update/edit method, so the new endpoint is only reachable through raw fetch. The test also has to use raw() instead of the client.
findings.fix: Add `update: (id, text) => call('PATCH', `/notes/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`, { text })` to createClient. Use app.alice.update in the test.

pre_existing.issue: If the POST body is JSON `null`, readJson resolves null and body.text throws a TypeError, which returns a 500 instead of a 400.
